text:
Anika Singh: alert-bot just fired SLO burn for hosted-infer.gateway p99 timeouts, panels spiking in the last 10m :rotating_light:
ops-alert-bot: [ALERT] SLO: hosted-infer.gateway.p99_latency > 2s for 10m (service: hosted-infer-gateway)
Leo Chen: copying dashboards now, looks like a simultaneous jump in 5xx too based on quick glance
Sam Katz: is this affecting all regions or just us-east-1? users reporting timeouts from support ticket 4512
Maria Alvarez: support says ~30% of requests getting 502/504s, users see "upstream request timeout" in response body
Devon Park: ingress-proxy logs show a lot of upstream connect_timeouts around 1768401000 - 1768401200
Anika Singh: can someone run the query to see if this aligns with dedicated vs hosted model routes?
Leo Chen: running quick kql: index=ingress_logs service=hosted-infer | where timestamp >= now()-15m | stats count(), pctile(latency,95) by upstream_cluster
Leo Chen: result -> spike on cluster hosted-infer-runtime-1 and runtime-2, runtime-3 stable
Sam Katz: runtime-1 and runtime-2 are on the same AZ; could be capacity + noisy neighbor
Maria Alvarez: any deploys in last 30m? deploy-bot shows a canary to runtime-service 1.4.8 at 1768399800
Devon Park: yes, there was a canary. Canary succeeded but rollout continued. Reverting canary now to see if it helps
Anika Singh: before rollback, let's check traces for request path. Looks like span sampling dropped: trace-sampling=0.05 in prod which explains gaps
Leo Chen: traced one of the failing requests: long wait in "runtime-client" between send and response (~1.8s) then gateway times out at 2s. No obvious error in model-host logs
Sam Katz: model-hosts report elevated GC pauses? Checking node-exporter: java_gc_pause 0.3s average but some spikes to 2s around the window
Maria Alvarez: that could explain p99s. Are those model-hosts autoscaling properly?
Devon Park: autoscaler didn't kick: memory pressure threshold not hit because container capped CPU but GC blocks threads. We use heap tuning for inference JVM process; recent change increased maxHeap by 20% in 1.4.8
Anika Singh: ok, this smells like the canary that bumped heap + some request pattern causing longer stop-the-world GCs. Rollback done by Sam: 1.4.7 rolling back to stable 1.4.6 on runtime-1/2
Sam Katz: rollback started. Also enabling fallback routing to runtime-3 to absorb load: route-policy set to prefer runtime-3 on p99 degrade
Leo Chen: routing change pushed. Also temporary reduce concurrency per-worker: set MAX_INFLIGHT=8 for runtime pods via k8s patch
Maria Alvarez: support updated customers: "we're investigating increased timeouts, temporary mitigation in place. ETA 30-45m" :thumbsup:
Devon Park: after rollback and concurrency change, p95/p99 coming down. SLO alert cleared at 1768402100
ops-alert-bot: [RESOLVED] SLO: hosted-infer.gateway.p99_latency back within threshold
Anika Singh: follow-up: need an RCA and action items. Immediate ones I see - revert heap bump in canary, add GC metrics to SLO/alerting, increase trace sampling to 0.2 during incidents, and add autoscaler rule for long GC detection
Leo Chen: logging gap note: our trace-forwarder had a backpressure throttle earlier which dropped spans when collector lag > 5s. We need to ensure trace-backpressure doesn't blind SRE. Filing a ticket.
Sam Katz: I'll draft the incident summary and link dashboards + queries. Adding queries used below for reproducibility:

```
# ingestion query (KQL)
index=ingress_logs service=hosted-infer | where timestamp >= unix_time(1768401000) and timestamp <= unix_time(1768402200) | stats count(), pctile(latency,95), sum(status==502) as num_502 by upstream_cluster

# runtime JVM GC check
index=metrics metric=java_gc_pause | where host in (runtime-1,runtime-2) | stats max(value) as max_gc by host
```

Maria Alvarez: reopening support tickets with root cause and workaround notes. Also let's add a temporary health-check reroute for canary rollouts so we don't put 50% of an AZ under the new config
Devon Park: creating follow-up issues: INF-429 (revert heap bump), INF-430 (GC-aware autoscaling), INF-431 (increase trace sampling on SLO alerts), INF-432 (canary isolation policy)
Anika Singh: schedule postmortem in 24h, include runtime and deployment owners. Also add a dashboard panel correlating deploys with p99 jumps
Leo Chen: one more note: billing/auth checks looked normal, so not auth throttles. Saw a handful of 401s unrelated to this spike
Sam Katz: good catch. Closing thread after I attach graphs and timeline to INF-429. Thanks everyone :clap:
